title: bonsai.agents/1
description: bonsai agents --json (set 8; plan-5 5.5.12): the one published view of what Bonsai has recorded about each agent in a project, for the studio's agent screen: each agent's role, parent, task, brief, last call, counts and limits, report and token counts, copied as recorded. Its rule: it interprets nothing, predicts nothing and does no needless arithmetic: no derived state, share, cost or estimate, and no minutes worked out against the clock; the studio computes those from last_call.at, ended, the counts and the limits. Bonsai's own state files under .bonsai/local/agents/ stay internal, with no format; this is their only published shape. It reads only and never acts: it never starts, wakes or stops an agent. Printed, never stored. What was recorded under each agent's name is attributed, not authenticated: not proof that agent did it. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null, [] or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

workspace.description: The workspace: its id and name from bonsai.yaml, and the main checkout's absolute path, forward slashes (printed locally, never stored or forwarded); null when the command refused before reading bonsai.yaml.

root.description: The checkout's absolute path, forward slashes.

agents.description: Every agent the generated kind agents still keeps, the person's own sessions among them, sorted by started, then id; each copied as recorded, field by field. [] when none is recorded; in a project whose packs declare no roles, the person's sessions alone.

id.description: The agent's id: Claude Code's agent_id for a subagent, the session's id for a top-level session (the person's own, or a named session).

session.description: The session it ran in: a top-level session's own id, or the session that started a subagent.

parent.description: Who started it, as its spawn record names it: session for an agent the person's own session started (and for one a Workflow script started, whose Workflow call only that session makes), the starting agent's id for one a lead started; null for the person's own session and for a named session, whose starter Bonsai does not see. The tree of agents is rebuilt from parent alone.

role.description: The declared role it plays (bonsai.pack/1's roles[].name), or null for a type no linked pack declares (Explore, Plan, general-purpose, a fork), which the guard holds as a helper.

type.description: Claude Code's agent type, as its hooks gave it; null for a top-level session started with no agent.

task.description: The task it served: its tied brief's, or a named session's BONSAI_TASK; null for none.

brief.description: The id of the brief tied to it, the one in force; null for none.

model.description: The model, where a record names one (the session's start, the newest usage record); null where none does.

started.description: When the guard first saw it (its first call), or a top-level session's start: ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds; null where no record holds it.

ended.description: When it ended, from its stop record (subagent_stop, or its session's session_end); null while none is recorded.

last_call.description: Its last tool call, as the log records it; null before its first.

at.description: When the call was made: ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds.

category.description: The tool's category, the log's open list (bonsai.log/1's category); null where the record names none.

counts.description: Its counts as the guard wrote them (step 5.5.11): minutes, the figure on its last call line; actions, the call lines since its window's start (its first call, or its newest brief's tie); red_runs, from its last red or reset line. Never worked out again here. null for the person's own session, which the guard never counts.

minutes.description: Minutes, as the guard measured them when it judged the agent's last call; null before its first call line.

actions.description: Tool calls since its window's start, refused ones counted.

red_runs.description: Failed ladder runs in a row, as its last red or reset line says.

limits.description: The limits that bound it, as the guard wrote them on its start or last tie line: the brief's where it gave one (a brief's actions: 5 shows 5), else the role's defaults in force then, never today's. null for the person's own session, which has none.

minutes.description: The minutes limit that bounded it (minutes since the agent's first call, or since it tied its newest brief (its thinking before its first call is not counted; time idle between calls is)): its value in force and its max.

value.description: The value in force: the brief's where it gave one, else the default in force; null for no limit.

max.description: The max in force when it was written; null for no limit.

actions.description: The actions limit that bounded it (tool calls the agent makes, refused ones counted, from the same start): its value in force and its max.

value.description: The value in force: the brief's where it gave one, else the default in force; null for no limit.

max.description: The max in force when it was written; null for no limit.

red_runs.description: The red_runs limit that bounded it (failed ladder runs in a row (a green climb sets the count back to 0; a new brief does not)): its value in force and its max.

value.description: The value in force: the brief's where it gave one, else the default in force; null for no limit.

max.description: The max in force when it was written; null for no limit.

spent.description: true once the guard has recorded its budget spent; false otherwise. A recorded fact, never worked out here.

report.description: Its report: the newest report whose from is its own address (its tied brief's to), by its id and status; a report written from another address is never shown. null for none.

status.description: The report's status, bonsai.message/1's closed list but null.

log.description: Its log file, project-relative in the main checkout, forward slashes; null when none is kept.

thread.description: The thread of its tied brief; null for none.

usage.description: Its token counts, raw, as its newest usage records hold them: one item a model, the whole transcript's totals at its newest end, copied and never summed across records (a resumed agent's newest records hold its whole transcript); or one item, kind unknown with its reason, when that end's transcript could not be read. null until its first usage record exists. No cost and no estimate.

model.description: The model, as Claude Code named it in the transcript; null on an unknown item.

input.description: The input tokens, summed over the whole transcript, as the usage record holds them; null on an unknown item.

output.description: The output tokens, summed over the whole transcript, as the usage record holds them; null on an unknown item.

cache_read.description: The tokens read from the cache, summed over the whole transcript, as the usage record holds them; null on an unknown item.

cache_write.description: The tokens written to the cache, summed over the whole transcript, as the usage record holds them; null on an unknown item.

kind.description: null for counts read from the transcript; unknown when it could not be read: the usage record's kind.

reason.description: Why the transcript could not be read, the usage record's reason; null otherwise.
examples: the transcript's layout is not one Bonsai reads

skipped.description: Each state file under .bonsai/local/agents/ that could not be read: its path and why. It is skipped, never an error for the rest, and never shown with counts it does not hold. [] for none.

examples.reason: its first line is not a start line

path.description: The state file, project-relative in the main checkout, forward slashes.

reason.description: Why it could not be read, one sentence.
examples: its first line is not a start line

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
